Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

long adverb

for a long time

also for a long time, a long time, for long, longer, all this time, for ages

classical

Cic. Fam. 7.9.1: jam diū ignōrō quid agās
Ter. Hec. 84: ubi tē oblectāstī tam diū?

diū

adverb; comparative diūtius, superlative diūtissimē

long, for a long time

Jam diū with the present is “for a long time now”, as in Cicero’s jam diū ignōrō. Tam diū, so long; quam diū?, how long? (see how long?); diūtius, longer, any longer. Long ago is ōlim or jam prīdem.

Other words

  • longum tempus — a long time

    noun with adjective · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 4.1.1: post longum tempus; Plin. NH 18.83: longō tempore

    When the time itself is named: post longum tempus, after a long time.

Examples

  • jam diū ignōrō quid agās; nihil enim scrībis

    I’ve had no idea for ages how you are; you never writeCic. Fam. 7.9.1

  • Dīc mihi, Philōtis, ubi tē oblectāstī tam diū?

    Tell me, Philotis, where have you been enjoying yourself all this time?Ter. Hec. 84

See also how long?, it won’t be long, finally, ago, long.
